content.thinking:
This change swaps an O(n) computation for an O(n^2) one, recalculating spent_by_then from scratch for every purchase in the loop — that's CPU-bound and would scale badly with purchase count. The latency spike starting at 21:38 lines up exactly with the deploy timestamp, so this looks like a bad code deployment causing the issue, not a config or flag change.

The metrics back this up: p50 jumps above 300ms, p95 into 1494-2230ms, p99 into 2709-3940ms, while error rates stay low (~1% with occasional client disconnects from timeouts) — consistent with an expensive computation slowing responses rather than crashing them. CPU usage, CPU limits, memory, and traffic all stay flat, ruling out autoscaling issues or demand saturation. The rollout also converged across all three replicas, ruling out an in-flight compatibility break.

Given the deploy timing matches the latency onset precisely and the code change explains the pattern well, I'm fairly confident (~0.9) this is a performance regression from the bad deployment.
